decision.state: Exploratory credential model; causal effect and marginal funding plan unverified
decision.summary: Five Keys operates accredited adult and non-traditional high-school programs alongside reentry, workforce, housing, and other services. Its FY2024 audit now supports a bounded FKIH cost per ADA-equivalent year, but Five Keys' public results still do not identify a comparable credential-completion group, complete post-release follow-up, incremental philanthropic cost, or the additional activity a private gift would buy. The published recidivism comparison remains a signal to investigate—not a causal effect or impact price.
decision.costEffectiveness: Exploratory: about $166,700 per additional credential at a modeled 10-point effect
decision.recommendation: Not recommendation-ready; a null remains plausible

financialContext.summary: The FY2024 audit reports $121.98 million in organization revenue, $120.78 million in expenses, and $39.81 million in net assets. Its combining schedules isolate $37.21 million of Five Keys Independence High expense and 2,232.74 annual ADA. The city's separate ledger has 15 active exact-name prime-contract records with $214.86 million of multiyear award authority and $136.42 million paid as of August 20, 2026.
financialContext.boundary: The organization spans schools, housing, workforce, reentry, and other programs. The audit permits a historical FKIH cost per ADA-equivalent year, but ADA is not unique enrollment, dosage, marginal seats, or completed credentials. City records are dominated by housing and homelessness services, use overlapping multiyear terms, and distinguish award authority, payments, outstanding purchase orders, and remaining authority. None of those fields is a private-donation gap, and none should be divided by graduates.

evidence.population: Five Keys students across accredited charter schools, community sites, and 17 county jails in California
evidence.result: Five Keys reports more than 2,100 graduates to date and says its schools operate at more than 51 community settings and in 17 jails. Its 2024–25 FKIH LCAP reports 56 people passed all GED portions in 2022–23, while its FY2024 audit reports 2,232.74 annual ADA.
evidence.transfer: These figures establish delivery and credential outputs, not impact. ADA is an attendance-based funding denominator rather than unique learner flow, and the public record does not publish a San Francisco-only cohort, eligible or tested GED denominator, comparable nonparticipant group, or complete post-release follow-up.

evidence.population: Five Keys graduates in San Francisco and participants receiving education plus intensive case management and cognitive-behavioral programming in Los Angeles
evidence.result: A Five Keys media kit reports 26% recidivism for San Francisco graduates and 17% for the Los Angeles bundled program, compared with a 60%–70% statewide figure.
evidence.transfer: The media kit does not publish cohort dates, sample sizes, eligibility, a common recidivism definition, follow-up completeness, risk adjustment, or a contemporaneous comparison. Graduates are selected completers, and the Los Angeles result combines multiple services. The comparison cannot be interpreted as a Five Keys causal reduction.

evidence.design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of U.S. correctional-education evaluations
evidence.population: Incarcerated adults in studies of adult basic, secondary/GED, postsecondary, and vocational education published from 1980 through 2011
evidence.result: RAND found 30% lower odds of recidivism in the high-school/GED subset. Across the full correctional-education evidence base, its modeled three-year reincarceration risk difference was 12.9 points, but programs, outcomes, follow-up, and study quality varied; RAND identified curriculum, dosage, and program quality as unresolved evidence gaps.
evidence.transfer: This supports correctional education as a promising intervention class, not Five Keys' effect size. The studies predate current Five Keys delivery, mix prison contexts and program types, and do not establish San Francisco implementation quality, marginal cost, or philanthropic additionality.

model.nativeOutcome: Additional eligible learner earning an accredited secondary credential and remaining out of custody for 24 months because of the funded Five Keys program
model.bestGuess: About $166,700 per additional credential, conditional on one ADA-equivalent year increasing credential completion by 10 percentage points
missingInputs: A named Five Keys school or program, legal and funding boundary, geography, and gift-restricted cohort
Unique eligible learners, applicants, enrollees, attendance or dosage, withdrawals, transfers, credentials, and duplicate handling
A pre-specified credential and recidivism outcome with arrest, conviction, jail, and prison definitions kept separate
Complete 6-, 12-, 24-, and 36-month post-release follow-up with release dates, attrition, and subgroup results
A credible Five Keys comparison or a transparent, sensitivity-tested transfer from external correctional-education evidence

Incremental instructional, navigation, case-management, facilities, custody-coordination, and overhead cost by program and cohort; the published $16,667 per ADA-equivalent year is historical schoolwide intensity
Public charter reimbursement, city and county contract coverage, service substitution, and private-gift additionality
Time-bounded $100K, $1M, and $10M capacity plans with seats, staffing, constraints, milestones, and downside cases
model.qalyBoundary: No QALY, WELLBY, life-saved, or life-substantially-bettered conversion is published. The exploratory model estimates additional credentials only. Avoided custody, education, earnings, safety, family, and wellbeing effects require separate causal estimates and must not be double-counted.

reservations: Five Keys combines accredited schools with reentry, workforce, housing, restorative-justice, and other services across multiple counties.
Cumulative graduates and annual GED completions are outputs without a reconciled eligible-student denominator or counterfactual.
The published 26% and 17% recidivism figures use an in-house comparison whose cohort, follow-up, and outcome definitions are not disclosed.
Comparing selected graduates with a statewide incarcerated population is vulnerable to selection, geography, calendar-time, and risk differences.
RAND's favorable intervention evidence is heterogeneous and does not identify Five Keys' curriculum, dosage, or local implementation effect.
The FY2024 audit isolates FKIH expense and ADA, but dividing those values yields only a historical cost per ADA-equivalent year—not cost per unique learner, marginal seat, or additional credential.
Public school funding and large service contracts may fund overlapping inputs; the extra activity and displacement created by a private gift are unknown.
